payload.fact: The amount of attorneys' fees and costs the D. Del. court fixes against ChromaDex in favour of Elysium Health (1:18-cv-01434), and its ruling date.
payload.why_pivotal: At the ~$9.8M ceiling every fee-award path leaves ChromaDex short of the $17.78M lowest cash the $2.0M request needs, so the event-adjusted recommendation falls to $1.43M. A lower fixed amount raises the event-adjusted limit.
payload.acceptable_evidence: D. Del. order fixing the fee amount; company disclosure (8-K/10-Q) of the ruled amount.
payload.if_resolved: If the award is roughly $0.9M+ below $9.8M, the pay/settle paths clear the $2.0M request (appeal-bond cash-collateral paths still depend on security form). If the award is at or near $9.8M, $1.43M stays the maximum.

payload.fact: How ChromaDex would secure a stay pending its intended appeal of the Delaware fee award: cash collateral (and what share), or a surety bond or letter of credit that does not lock cash.
payload.why_pivotal: The appeal-with-stay paths lock $6.1M–$12.25M of modelled cash collateral and produce the lowest projected cash ($12.7M). These are the binding paths for the event-adjusted limit.
payload.acceptable_evidence: Management confirmation or bond/LC documentation; revolver LC capacity terms.
payload.if_resolved: A non-cash bond or letter of credit removes the lock, and only the pay/settle paths bind. A cash-collateralised bond keeps the limit near $1.43M.

payload.fact: Whether the Western Alliance Credit Agreement's additional-indebtedness and minimum-cash/liquidity covenants permit $2.0M (or $1.43M) of unsecured Slope bill-pay financing without consent, and whether ChromaDex is in compliance.
payload.why_pivotal: Slope policy requires that existing lenders' covenants permit the financing. A covenant breach could block revolver access or trigger an event of default.
payload.acceptable_evidence: Credit Agreement Exhibit 10.2 permitted-indebtedness basket, lender consent letter, or latest compliance certificate.
payload.if_resolved: If it is permitted, the financing proceeds at the scenario-supported amount. If it is not, decline until Western Alliance consents.

payload.fact: Whether and when Elysium paid the $2,500,000 owed to ChromaDex under the 13 Aug 2024 C.D. Cal. judgment (Dkt. 618).
payload.why_pivotal: Receipt raises lowest projected cash by up to $2.5M and narrows the shortfall. It is not counted until received.
payload.acceptable_evidence: Connected-bank inflow from Elysium or company confirmation of receipt.
payload.if_resolved: Once received, the cash enters the connected-bank data. On its own it does not close the shortfall on the fee-award paths.

payload.summary:
ChromaDex requested $2.0M of Slope bill-pay financing (90 days, 3 monthly installments) for a Tru Niagen contract-manufacturer invoice, reviewed as of 19 Aug 2024. Tier A. Bank-only view: the $2.0M request passes (limit $3.62M, order limit $2.72M, lowest projected cash $24.96M). Two live Elysium disputes were compiled.
(1) C.D. Cal. 8:16-cv-02277 Dkt. 618, entered 13 Aug 2024: Elysium must pay ChromaDex $2,500,000. The judgment bars post-trial motions and appeals on the Jury Claims, each party bears its own fees, and the court keeps enforcement jurisdiction for 120 days. No payment date is stated and receipt is unconfirmed.
(2) D. Del. 1:18-cv-01434: on 25 Mar 2024 the court granted Elysium's motion for attorneys' fees and costs against ChromaDex. The amount was fully briefed by 13 Jun 2024 and awaits a ruling. ChromaDex intends to appeal, and management puts the exposure at about $9.8M including estimated post-judgment interest (reasonably possible, not accrued).
The Western Alliance revolver (up to $10.0M, maturing 12 Nov 2025) was undrawn at 30 Jun 2024. Its covenants restrict additional indebtedness and cover cash kept at the bank, and it is secured by collateral. Management says covenant compliance is not assured. Purchase obligations of $9.0M and lease obligations of $3.4M are already in the baseline outflows.
Event-adjusted run_scenarios: $2.0M fails the order limit. The largest passing structure is inst_90 at $1,430,000; the order limit is about $1.43M, set by lowest projected cash. The binding paths are the fee award fixed at $9.8M with ChromaDex appealing and cash-collateralising a stay bond. The requested amount needs $17.78M of lowest projected cash on every path, and every fee-award path falls short by at least $0.85M.
pivotal_unknowns: Amount and timing of the D. Del. 1:18-cv-01434 attorneys' fees and costs award against ChromaDex (currently $0 to ~$9.8M; fully briefed, awaiting ruling)
Form of stay security if ChromaDex appeals the fee award (cash collateral vs surety bond/letter of credit)
Whether the Western Alliance Bank Credit Agreement's additional-indebtedness and liquidity covenants permit the Slope financing without consent
Whether/when Elysium paid the $2.5M owed to ChromaDex under C.D. Cal. Dkt. 618 (not relied upon)
payload.conclusion:
Based on run_scenarios, the requested $2.0M, 90-day installment financing passes on the bank-only view but not on the event-adjusted view. The engine's recommended structure is inst_90 at $1,430,000 (3 monthly installments). Under the model's cash-collateral assumption, the lowest projected cash is about $12.7M, on the paths where the Delaware fee award is fixed and ChromaDex appeals with a cash-collateralised bond. The $2.0M request needs at least $17.78M of lowest projected cash on every path. Every fee-award path is short by at least $0.85M, whatever happens on the Elysium receivable.
The approval rests on three pivotal unknowns:
(a) the amount the D. Del. court fixes, which currently runs up to about $9.8M (the amount Elysium seeks plus estimated interest);
(b) whether a stay pending appeal would be secured with cash collateral or with a non-cash bond or letter of credit;
(c) whether the Western Alliance covenant on additional indebtedness permits the Slope financing without lender consent.
The $2.5M that Elysium owes ChromaDex under the 13 Aug 2024 judgment is counted only once received. The approval does not rely on it.
Material litigation is an exception-review trigger under Slope policy, so this case goes to human exception review. No offer is made and no account is changed.
